one_line: case studies timing how fast evidence reaches guidelines, labels and literature
skills: API data pipelines with rate-limit handling
data: PubMed title/abstract counts by year via NCBI E-utilities
ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (trial start years, MeSH-derived disease flags)
FDA approval history (hand-entered dates, marked unverified)

decisions.chose: PubMed title/abstract term counts by year
decisions.over: the ClinicalTrials.gov registry already pulled for this repo
decisions.because: the registry holds only a handful of relevant trials for these conditions and terms, and NICE-governed UK practice is largely never registered on a US registry
decisions.evidence: checked ClinicalTrials.gov first (already in this repo, no new pull needed) and it is too thin for this question

decisions.chose: weight-related FAERS reports as a share of all reports for the same drug
decisions.because: total FAERS volume grows every year on its own, so a raw count can ride that trend rather than show a drug-specific signal
decisions.evidence: Total FAERS volume grows every year regardless of any specific drug effect, so signal 1 needs to be read as a share of signal 2, not as a raw count.

decisions.chose: leaving patent evidence out of the GLP-1 cascade entirely
decisions.over: pulling patent text as a third signal of when the weight effect was known
decisions.because: there is no clean structured source for it and a weak proxy would be worse than an acknowledged gap
decisions.evidence: Patent text was not pulled at all; there is no clean structured API for it, and pretending to have signal there would be worse than leaving it out.

decisions.chose: one search term per script invocation, merged afterwards
decisions.over: one run pulling every term and year
decisions.because: a full sweep of fifty years by four terms at the unauthenticated NCBI rate does not finish inside a short shell timeout
decisions.evidence: One term per invocation, so a single run finishes inside a short shell timeout.

broke.what: the approval dates that carry the whole GLP-1 signal-versus-label figure were typed in by hand and are flagged as unverified against the labels
broke.evidence: Hand-entered from FDA approval history. VERIFY against the label before this figure goes anywhere public: these dates are the whole argument.

broke.what: figure footnotes placed below the axes were flagged as clipped by the repo's own figure audit, because the canvas only expands at save time
broke.evidence: text placed below the axes trips audit()'s clipped check, because bbox="tight" expands the canvas only at save time

broke.what: the ME/CFS case does not separate the guideline change from an earlier controversy, and the notebook says so rather than reading the trend as guideline lag
broke.evidence: The GET/pacing decline may be confounded with the separate PACE-trial reanalysis controversy (from around 2016), which predates and may be doing more work than NG206 itself.

question: How long does it take for a change in evidence or a safety signal to show up in guidelines, drug labels and the published literature?
rejected_line: Tried the trial registry first for the ME/CFS and EDS guideline questions; too few registered trials use the terms at all, so switched to PubMed term counts by year.
